thread.title: Hang Seng Likely To Give Up Support At 25,000 Points

title: Hang Seng Likely To Give Up Support At 25,000 Points
text:
Hang Seng Likely To Give Up Support At 25,000 Points 17: The Hong Kong stock market has finished lower in back-to-back trading days, sliding almost 800 points or 3 percent along the way. The Hang Seng Index now rests just above the 25,060-point plateau and it's called lower again on Friday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is broadly negative, with bad news from Apple expected to weigh heavily on technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were firmly in the red and the Asian bourses are expected to follow suit.
The Hang Seng finished slightly lower on Thursday as losses from the insurance companies were offset by support from the oil and property sectors.
For the day, the index sank 65.99 points or 0.26 percent to finish at 25,064.36 after trading between 24,896.87 and 25,262.21.
Among the actives, CSPC Pharmaceutical plummeted 5.81 percent, while AAC Technologies plunged 5.41 percent, Sino Land surged 4.41 percent, Sun Hung Kai Properties soared 2.94 percent, China Resources Land spiked 2.65 percent, CITIC jumped 2.53 percent, China Mengniu Dairy tumbled 2.31 percent, China Petroleum and Chemical (Sinopec) climbed 1.84 percent, BOC Hong Kong skidded 1.76 percent, AIA Group dropped 1.75 percent, WH Group retreated 1.73 percent, CNOOC advanced 1.41 percent, China Life Insurance was down 1.11 percent, China Mobile rose 0.95 percent, Galaxy Entertainment added 0.84 percent, Ping An Insurance shed 0.81 percent, Tencent Holdings lost 0.52 percent, Hong Kong & China Gas fell 0.49 percent, New World Development gained 0.39 percent, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China collected 0.18 percent and Sands China and Hengan International were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is brutal as stocks opened sharply lower on Thursday and remained that way throughout the session.
The Dow shed 660.02 points or 2.83 percent to 22,686.22, while the NASDAQ lost 202.43 points or 3.04 percent to 6,463.50 and the S&P fell 62.14 points or 2.48 percent to 2,447.89.
Downwardly revised guidance from Apple (AAPL) contributed to the early selloff on Wall Street, with the tech giant plunging 10 percent. The lower guidance was attributed to a greater than expected impact from economic weakness in some emerging markets and China.
In economic news, the Institute for Supply Management noted a bigger than expected slowdown in U.S. manufacturing activity in December. Also, payroll processor ADP reported much stronger than expected U.S. private sector job growth in December.
Crude oil prices extended gains to a fourth successive session Thursday on hopes the proposed reduction in oil output by OPEC will allay fears of excess supply in the market. Crude oil futures for February ended up $0.55 or 1.2 percent at $47.09 a barrel. //www.rttnews.com/2966807/hang-seng-likely-to-give-up-support-at-25000-points.aspx
